description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Madeleine Dean of Pennsylvania (D) states the Trump administration lacks a clear roadmap in Iran, warning escalation risks more US casualties. Rep. Nick LaLota of New York (R) says he's open to any bipartisan deal to end the DHS shutdown and restore TSA pay. Mara Rudman, professor at the University of Virginia’s Miller Center, discusses differences between public US and Iran messaging and behind-the-scenes engagement. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Faces Fresh Iran Demands in Bid to Jump-Start Talks | Balance of Power: Late Edition 03/25/26

author: Jessica Nix, Rachel Cohrs Zhang
description: The Trump administration is expected to miss a deadline to name a new director for the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, leaving the public health agency without a leader and adding to its leadership turmoil.
title: CDC Left Without Director After White House Misses Key Deadline

description: Lloyd Blankfein, the former chairman and CEO of Goldman Sachs, remains wary of systemic "kindling" despite a banking sector that is currently better capitalized than in previous crises. In an interview with Bloomberg's Francine Lacqua, he weighs the "balancing act" of Donald Trump’s policy outcomes against the unpredictability of the global energy supply. Blankfein warns that the long absence of a market reckoning has allowed private equity inventory to accumulate like tinder. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Lloyd Blankfein on Private Equity, Trump, and Next Global Reckoning

author: Hadriana Lowenkron, Saleha Mohsin, Eric Martin
description: Trump administration officials are examining what a potential spike in oil prices as high as $200 a barrel would mean for the economy, according to people familiar with the matter, a sign senior officials are studying the possible fallout from extreme scenarios for the Iran war.
title: Trump Team Examines What Oil as High as $200 a Barrel Would Mean

description: Mara Rudman, professor at the University of Virginia’s Miller Center and former deputy envoy for Middle East peace at the US State Department, discusses differences between public US and Iran messaging and behind-the-scenes engagement, the officials involved in negotiations, and the buildup of US military assets in the region. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fmr. US State Dept. Envoy on Iran Talks, Military Buildup

description: Rep. Nick LaLota of New York, a retired US Navy lieutenant and member of the House Appropriations and Homeland Security Committees, says showcasing US military strength is critical to backing diplomacy with Iran while downplaying the likelihood of ground troops. He also says he's open to any bipartisan deal to end the DHS shutdown and restore TSA pay. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. LaLota Says Military Pressure Key to Iran Diplomacy, Signals DHS Deal Openness

description: Rep. Madeleine Dean of Pennsylvania tells Bloomberg’s Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu the administration lacks a clear roadmap in Iran, warning escalation risks more US casualties. She also criticizes stalled Capitol Hill negotiations to end the DHS shutdown. She speaks on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Dean Says Iran Conflict Still a 'Reckless War of Choice'

author: Courtney McBride, Jen Judson
description: Even as Donald Trump pushes for talks to end the war against Iran, the US has ordered thousands of troops to the region, fueling fears that the president is gearing up for exactly the sort of risky ground invasion that he once campaigned against.
title: US Troop Movements Fan Fears of a Risky Ground Attack on Iran

author: Sherif Tarek, Fiona MacDonald
description: Kuwait said it had arrested another group affiliated with Hezbollah, foiling a terror plot that called for the assassination of leaders and senior officials in the Gulf state.
title: Kuwait Arrests More Suspects in Plot to Assassinate Leaders

author: Zoe Tillman
description: US Justice Department lawyers told a federal judge that they’ve been relying on incorrect information for months in a fight over the Trump administration’s migrant arrest tactics, and blamed Immigration and Customs Enforcement for the “regrettable error.”
title: DOJ Blames ICE for ‘Regrettable Error’ in Immigration Lawsuit

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss Meta and Google being found liable in a landmark court case about social media addiction. Bloomberg News Legal Analyst June Grasso weighs in. Then, Bloomberg News Middle East Reporter Dan Williams as US-Iran truce talks hang in the balance. Plus, Bloomberg News White House & National Security Editor Michelle Jamrisko as the White House pushes back on details about a potential peace plan. Then, Prologis CEO Dan Letter discusses the state of global logistics. Finally, Bloomberg News AI Reporter Rachel Metz joins to discuss OpenAI discontinuing its video app Sora. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Meta, Google Found Liable in Social Media Addiction Case | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/25/2026

author: Nancy Cook
description: If the economy falters, political pressure on the president will build.
title: Trump Confronting Economic Stresses From War With Iran

author: Chris Strohm
description: The Federal Reserve made its next move in a legal battle over US Justice Department subpoenas obtained as part of an investigation into building renovations overseen by Chair Jerome Powell, setting the stage for an appeal by the side that loses.
title: Federal Reserve Makes Next Move in Battle Over DOJ Subpoenas

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from the Middle East. On today's show, Republican Congressman Marlin Stutzman, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Bellwether Government Affairs CEO Arshi Siddiqui and CSIS Middle East Program Director Mona Yacoubian. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Rejects Trump Outreach | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/25/2026

author: Carla Samon Ros
description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum is working to develop climate models that will help prevent extreme weather events, part of a push to set up a public supercomputer that can use millions of data points to tackle national challenges.
title: Mexico Bets on Supercomputer to Combat Extreme Weather Events

description: President Donald Trump will meet China's Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 14-15. Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt broke the news to Bloomberg's Mario Parker during the White House briefing on Wednesday. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Will Go To China for Summit With Xi on May 14-15

description: Representative Marlin Stutzman, an Indiana Republican, pushed back on the idea that the SAVE act - a voter ID measure - and DHS funding should be linked. The congressman said that combining the two into one bill is confusing and that lawmakers have to be 'straight up with the American people' that the issues can be handled separately. Stutzman also talked about the ongoing war in Iran and its impact on his constituents. He said that despite the rise in gasoline prices because of the war with Iran, most people in the US understand the need to deal with the threat posed by Iran.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Indiana Republican Says SAVE Act Does Not Have to be Paired With DHS Funding

description: Mona Yacoubian, director and senior adviser of the Middle East Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, said that Iran believes it holds 'some very important cards' and is still looking to exact as much leverage as possible over the war with the US. Yacoubian said that its hard to know what the Trump administration is thinking in regards to its Iran strategy, as press secretary Karoline Leavitt told reporters negotiations are ongoing amid more troop movement to the region.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Insists Talks Ongoing Even as Iran Rejects Plan

author: Zoe Tillman
description: The Justice Department has reached a financial settlement with Michael Flynn, a conservative activist and former official in the first Trump administration who sought millions of dollars from the government for what he alleged was a wrongful prosecution effort.
title: DOJ Agrees to Pay Ex-Trump Adviser Michael Flynn in Settlement

author: Donato Paolo Mancini
description: Italian Tourism Minister Daniela Santanchè has stepped down nearly a day after Premier Giorgia Meloni demanded her resignation in a bid to clean house in the wake of a bruising referendum defeat.
title: Italy Minister Steps Down After Meloni Demands Resignation

author: Josh Wingrove, Mario Parker
description: President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping will hold their highly anticipated summit in Beijing on May 14-15, following a delay that brought fresh uncertainty to relations between the world’s largest economies.
title: Trump to Travel to China on May 14-15 for Summit With Xi

author: Erik Wasson, Steven T. Dennis
description: Senate Republicans have rejected Democrats’ latest bid to end a lengthy shutdown at the Department of Homeland Security, prolonging a stalemate that has wreaked havoc on air travel and threatens to ripple through an economy already roiled by the Iran war.
title: Senate GOP Rejects Democrats’ Latest Bid to End DHS Shutdown

author: Alessandra Migliaccio, Donato Paolo Mancini
description: The Italian government is set to cut its economic growth forecast, reflecting a hit from the war in the Persian Gulf.
title: Italy Said to Plan Cutting Growth Forecast to as Low as 0.5%

author: Sanne Wass
description: Denmark will start talks to form a ruling coalition with caretaker Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen moving closer to securing a third term in office after winning backing from other party leaders to lead the negotiations.
title: Danish Coalition-Building Talks Start as Premier Gets First Stab

author: Mario Parker
description: President Donald Trump, roughly halfway through his five-day deadline to make a deal with Iran, faces fresh demands from Tehran to end a war that’s wreaked havoc across the Middle East and global markets.
title: Trump Faces Fresh Iran Demands in Bid to Jump-Start Talks

description: Netflix Inc.’s push into livestreaming mega events in Asia is set to accelerate, buoyed by hits from the World Baseball Classic to BTS’s comeback show that drew in waves of new, younger viewers. Bloomberg's Geetha Ranganathan joins to discuss Netflix as well as the recent news from Disney. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Netflix Bolsters Live Streaming With Splashy WBC, BTS Events

description:
Iran said it rejected a US ceasefire proposal and maintained attacks on Israel and Gulf Arab states, delivering a blow to Washington’s efforts to end a war.
Tehran has its own conditions for a ceasefire, including guarantees that the US and Israel won’t resume their attacks, alongside reparations for war damages and recognition of its authority over the Strait of Hormuz.
The US has compiled a peace proposal that includes Iran dismantling its main nuclear facilities and using a reduced missile arsenal in self-defense only, in exchange for certain concessions, including sanctions relief. Bloomberg's Dan Williams joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Rejects US Peace Plan in Blow to Efforts to End War

author: Michael Smith
description: Armando Labrador compone canciones, organiza concursos de belleza y lidera un grupo de disidentes que lleva a cabo protestas en La Habana. ¿Cuál podría ser su próximo paso? La presidencia de Cuba.
title: Dueño de una clínica de cirugías plásticas en Miami sueña con gobernar Cuba

author: Jorge Valero
description: The head of the International Energy Agency will participate in a meeting of European Union finance ministers this week as they craft possible responses to the war in the Middle East.
title: IEA Chief to Brief EU Finance Ministers on War Impact This Week

author: Myles Miller
description: The Transportation Security Administration warned new airport screeners won’t be ready in time for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, as the agency grapples with staffing shortages during a prolonged Department of Homeland Security shutdown.
title: TSA Warns New Airport Screeners Won’t Be Ready for World Cup

author: Lisa Beyer, Marissa Newman
description: The power of its air force diminished by Western sanctions, Iran invested heavily in missiles and drones over the years, amassing what US intelligence called in early 2025 the “largest stockpile” of such systems in the Middle East. Its capabilities are both a target of the war on Iran being waged by the US and Israel, which have long aimed to neutralize this threat, and Iran’s main means of responding to the assault.
title: What Are Iran’s Missile and Drone Capabilities?

author: Michael Smith
description: Armando Labrador writes songs, holds beauty pageants and leads a group of dissidents who stage protests in Havana. He sees a run for Cuba’s presidency in his future.
title: He Runs a Miami Plastic Surgery Clinic and Wants to Be Cuba's Next Leader

author: Dan Williams, Salma El Wardany, Donato Paolo Mancini, Josh Wingrove
description: US President Donald Trump’s plan to end the war with Iran stipulates that the Islamic Republic dismantle its main nuclear facilities and use a reduced missile arsenal in self-defense only, according to several people familiar with the matter.
title: US Demands Iran Dismantle Nuclear Sites as Part of Rejected 15-Point Plan

author: Ilya Arkhipov
description: Russian President Vladimir Putin accepted an invitation to visit Vietnam this year at Kremlin talks with Vietnamese Prime Minister Pham Minh Chinh.
title: Putin Says He Will Visit Vietnam in 2026 at Talks With Premier

author: Courtney Subramanian
description: President Donald Trump appointed industry titans including Mark Zuckerberg of Meta Platforms Inc., venture capitalist Marc Andreessen, Oracle Corp.’s Larry Ellison and Nvidia Corp.’s Jensen Huang to a new presidential technology council that will focus on artificial intelligence policy and other science-related issues.
title: Trump Taps Zuckerberg, Andreessen and Huang for Tech Council

author: Donato Paolo Mancini, Alberto Brambilla
description: Giorgia Meloni is seeking to boost gas flows from Algeria, as Italy and Spain vie to secure more North African energy to cushion the loss of Middle Eastern supplies choked off by the Iran war.
title: Italy’s Meloni Seeks to Boost Gas Flows From Algeria

author: Erik Wasson
description: On March 25, the partial US government shutdown affecting the Department of Homeland Security reached its 40th day.
title: Why ICE Is Being Paid During the Shutdown But TSA Is Not

author: Antonia Mufarech, James Attwood
description: Fuel pumps are running dry in parts of Chile as drivers rush to tank up before prices jump by as much as 54% Thursday. Angered by the fuel price hikes, some Chileans on Wednesday evening banged pots while student protests briefly shut a key metro line in the capital Santiago.
title: Fuel Price Hikes in Chile Test Kast as Supporters Start to Balk

description: Iran rejected a ceasefire proposal and called US talks “illogical,” according to the nation’s semi-official news agency Fars. But it's not clear who's doing the negotiating for Iran. Col. Wayne Sanders (Ret.) of Bloomberg Intelligence weighs in with more. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Who's Really in Charge of Iran?

description: Senator Dave McCormick, a Republican from Pennsylvania and member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, says the US has made “enormous progress” in the war with Iran. He speaks about negotiations between the two nations, the “optionality” created for President Donald Trump with US troops amassing in the Middle East, the reaction of financial and oil markets to the conflict, and his support for funding Homeland Security to end the partial government shutdown. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Senator McCormick Sees ‘More Work to Do’ on US Goals in Iran

author: S'thembile Cele
description: South Africa’s police chief was summoned to appear in court over his alleged role in a 360 million-rand ($21 million) health-services tender scandal, escalating scrutiny of the country’s top law enforcement office.
title: South Africa’s Police Chief Faces Charges Over Health Tender

author: Manolo Serapio Jr
description: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed on Wednesday a law that authorizes him to suspend or reduce the excise tax on petroleum products as the war in Iran keeps fuel prices elevated.
title: Philippines’ Marcos Signs Law to Halt Oil Tax Ahead of Transport Strike

author: Jorge Valero
description: The European Union will locate its new customs agency in Lille, France, a key step in the bloc’s push to harmonize the bloc’s rules and tackle an influx of cheap packages from China.
title: EU to Build Customs Agency in Lille as Chinese Parcels Surge

author: James Booth
description: The UK’s Financial Reporting Council is set to cut the number of inspections it carries out at major audit firms in what it calls a proportionate approach, as the watchdog pivots toward supporting the government’s economic growth agenda.
title: UK to Ease Oversight of Big Audit Firms in Starmer’s Growth Push

author: Thomas Seal
description: A separatist drive in Alberta could split a country that Trump wants to make the 51st US state.
title: In Oil-Rich Canadian Province, a Long-Shot Secession Bid Gains Traction

author: Kamil Kowalcze
description: Germany’s Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil wants to force foreign companies to form joint ventures with local firms to operate within Europe, while also seeking tighter scrutiny over cross-border takeovers.
title: German Finance Chief Seeks Joint Venture Rule for Foreign Firms

author: Charlie Duxbury
description: Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson’s chances to win another term in power got a boost after voter support for a junior coalition partner rose six months ahead of a general election.
title: Swedish Leader’s Election Bid Aided by Junior Partner Poll Bump

author: Alex Morales
description: The UK government plans to provide support for household energy bills after a cap on what utilities can charge expires at the end of June, UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said.
title: UK Plans ‘Appropriate’ Aid for Household Energy Bills After June

author: Marton Kasnyik
description: The mood in Hungary’s households lifted only slightly in March as Prime Minister Viktor Orban’s primed pre-election spending kicked in, but sentiment remains weaker than ahead of previous elections just as his Fidesz party faces its toughest challenge.
title: Hungary Consumer Sentiment Uptick Offers Little Boost For Orban

author: Sara Sjolin, Sanne Wass, Christian Wienberg
description: Denmark’s headstrong Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen holds the keys to deciding who becomes the Nordic nation’s next prime minister.
title: Danish Foreign Minister Becomes Kingmaker After Trump Standoff

author: Golnar Motevalli
description: As US President Donald Trump doubles down on his claim that he’s negotiating with Iran to end the war in the Persian Gulf, a conservative politician of the Islamic Republic has emerged as his most likely counterpart.
title: Iran’s Potential Peace Negotiator Known for Strongman Approach

author: Courtney McBride
description: The Pentagon has agreed with major defense contractors on a series of framework agreements meant to accelerate production of key missile systems that have seen heavy use during the initial phases of the US and Israeli war against Iran.
title: Pentagon Inks Deals to Boost Production of Key Weapons

author: Alex Morales
description: The Welsh nationalists of Plaid Cymru are set to overtake Labour to become the biggest party in Wales for the first time since 1999’s devolution, YouGov found in a survey that lays bare the danger to Prime Minister Keir Starmer posed by local elections in May.
title: Nationalists Poised to Win Wales and Push Labour Into Third

author: Tom Redmond, Anders Melin, Niki Koswanage
description: A senior leader in Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s party denied soliciting and receiving a bribe from businessman Victor Chin as the fallout from the so-called corporate mafia scandal intensifies in the Southeast Asian country.
title: Malaysia Cabinet Minister Denies Receiving $2.4 Million Bribe

author: Jonathan Tamari, Tina Davis
description: Real action begins as lawmakers face the prospect of missed flights home
title: DHS Funding Deal Begins With Declaring Victory, Then Negotiating

author: Jenni Marsh
description: The war is working out well for the Chinese leader but further out things may get trickier.
title: Xi Is Content to Stay Silent as Trump’s Iran War Backfires

author: Alfred Cang, Weilun Soon
description: Vessels seeking to transit the Strait of Hormuz under Iranian protection are being asked to provide lists of crew and cargo, along with voyage details and bills of lading, in order to secure a green light from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
title: Iran Demands Crew, Cargo Details to Send Ships Through Hormuz

description: Nataliia Lipikhina, EMEA equity strategy head at JPMorgan Private Bank, discusses the impact of the Iran war on global markets. "We still actually remain quite constructive on the market," Lipikhina tells Bloomberg Television. "We're seeing around 7,500 on S&P, and that is predicated on the fact that the recent geopolitical developments are actually a short-term headwind." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: JPM Sees S&P at 7,500 in 2026 If Iran War Short-Lived

author: Andrew Rosati
description: Flavio Bolsonaro edged ahead of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in the run-up to October’s election, with a new poll showing for the first time that the right-wing senator is leading the race.
title: Flavio Bolsonaro Inches Ahead of Lula in Brazil Election Poll

description: Oil fell as a diplomatic push by the US to try to end the war with Iran gathered pace despite the Strait of Hormuz remaining largely shut and news of more US troops being sent to the region. Oil remains on track for a substantial monthly surge after a volatile run of trading as investors tracked the fallout from the war. Bloomberg’s Anthony di Paola reports.
title: Oil Down as Trump Awaits Iran’s Response to Peace Plan

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, Bloomberg understands that the US drafted a 15-point plan that was delivered to Iran via Pakistan. Brent dipped below $100 and stocks climbed on optimism about Washington’s efforts to end the war.

Meanwhile, the Pentagon is said to be deploying about 2,000 troops to the Middle East.

Danish PM Mette Frederiksen’s party won a closely contested election shaped by Trump’s Greenland threats. But the party fell short of a majority, portending difficult coalition talks.

Today's guests: Hargreaves Lansdown Chief Investment Strategist Emma Wall (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War: US Forms 15-Point Plan to End War as Trump Pushes Talks | Daybreak Europe 3/25/2026

author: Arsalan Shahla
description: Iran kept up missiles and drone attacks on Arab Gulf states and Israel overnight, after the US floated a proposal to end a war that’s wreaked havoc across the Middle East and in global markets.
title: US Awaits Response to Peace Plan as Iran Keeps Up Attacks

description: Air travel disruption in the Middle East is ongoing and some carriers have halted passenger flights to destinations such as Dubai, Riyadh, and Tel Aviv. Bloomberg's Leen Al-Rashdan breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Air Travel Disruption in the Middle East Continues

author: Ott Tammik, Aaron Eglitis
description: Several drones entered Estonian and Latvian airspace from Russia on Wednesday morning, authorities said, adding that there were no injuries.
title: Drones Enter Baltic Airspace, Hitting Power Plant in Estonia

description: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen’s party won a closely contested election, setting the stage for difficult coalition talks to secure a third term in power. The premier’s Social Democrats emerged as the biggest party with 21.9% of the parliamentary vote after all ballots were preliminarily counted. The election was dominated by foreign and security policy in light of US President Donald Trump’s designs for Greenland. Bloomberg’s Sara Sjolin reports.
title: Danish Premier Wins Vote, Fails to Secure Majority

author: Soo-Hyang Choi
description: South Korea has begun rolling out its homegrown fighter jet, positioning the aircraft as a cheaper alternative to Lockheed Martin Corp.’s F-35 as the war in Iran prompts Gulf nations to scramble to build up their defenses.
title: South Korea Debuts Fighter Jet in Defense Push as Iran War Rages

description: Iran said foreign ships are allowed to cross the Strait of Hormuz, as long as they aren’t supporting acts of aggression against the country and follow regulations put in place by Tehran. The comments were made in a letter circulated to members of the International Maritime Organization. Bloomberg’s Joumanna Bercetche reports.
title: Iran Says Non-Hostile Foreign Ships Can Cross Hormuz

description: Palestinians inspect the wreckage of an Iranian missile in Kifl Haris, West Bank, on March 24. Photographer: Kobi Wolf/Bloomberg
title: US Bid for Talks With Iran Stirs Cautious Optimism

description: The European Union’s ​foreign affairs and security policy chief Kaja Kallas signed a new security pact with Ghana, designed to deepen cooperation on counter-terrorism, intelligence-sharing, crisis response and border and maritime security. As part of her trip to West Africa, Kallas also unveiled new deals with Nigeria. Bloomberg’s Jennifer Zabasajja reports.
title: EU Deepens West Africa Engagement

author: Rosalind Mathieson
description: The US is increasingly concerned at the emergence of “foreigner butchering” scams allegedly being run from China, adding another potential wrinkle to President Donald Trump’s planned meeting with Xi Jinping in the coming months.
title: US Worried by Rise in ‘Foreigner Butchering’ Scams From China

author: Ditas B Lopez
description: A Philippine congressional panel on Wednesday ordered the ombudsman to produce the statements of assets and liabilities of Vice President Sara Duterte as it tackles the impeachment complaints against her.
title: Philippine House Orders Submission of VP Duterte’s Asset Records

author: Nectar Gan
description: Hong Kong police reportedly arrested a bookstore owner and three employees on suspicion of selling “seditious” publications, including a biography of jailed media tycoon Jimmy Lai.
title: Hong Kong Arrests Booksellers Over Jimmy Lai Title, Reports Say

author: Sakura Murakami
description: An active officer of Japan’s Self-Defense Forces was arrested Tuesday after breaching the grounds of China’s embassy in Tokyo, prompting complaints from Beijing, in another episode likely to keep ties between Japan and China strained.
title: Japan Army Officer Arrested After Breaching Chinese Embassy

author: Josh Wingrove, Eric Martin, Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: The US has drafted a 15-point plan intended to help bring the war with Iran to a close, according to people familiar with the matter, highlighting the intensifying urgency within the Trump administration to resolve the conflict as the economic toll mounts.
title: US Forms 15-Point Plan to End Iran War as Trump Pushes Talks

author: John Harney
description: A Democrat is poised to represent President Donald Trump and his Mar-a-Lago residence in the Florida state House of Representatives after Republicans lost a special election in a surprise upset.
title: Democrats Flip Florida District Representing Trump’s Mar-a-Lago

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Jake Auchincloss, Democratic Congressman from Massachusetts, says US gains in air dominance have been offset by Iran's sea denial advantage. Barbara Leaf, Distinguished Diplomatic Fellow at the Middle East Institute, discusses prospects for US-Iran negotiations, leadership dynamics in Tehran, & risks around the Strait of Hormuz. Michael Claesson, Supreme Commander and Chief of Defense of the Swedish Armed Forces, talks about NATO's potential involvement in the Middle East conflict. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Sent Iran Plan to End Conflict: Reports  | Balance of Power: Late Edition 03/24/26

author: Pratik Parija, Ilena Peng, Eleanor Thornber
description: Governments are rushing to secure supplies of critical crop nutrients ahead of spring planting, as the Middle East war chokes off the flow of commodities and amplifies fears of a global food crisis.
title: Nations Race to Secure Enough Fertilizer and Prevent Food Crisis
